central_question: Can a logged collection configuration and replayable historical packet headers support intrusion-detector adaptation and prevent collection changes from being treated as traffic drift?
method: Configuration-matched replay: re-export a historical labeled packet-header reservoir under the deployed collection settings; fit a compact detector with equal total weight per communication window; calibrate alert thresholds per communication window; compare current traffic with a reference exported under the same settings.
unit: Canonical bidirectional IPv4 TCP/UDP five-tuple within a fixed 600-second capture-relative window. IP addresses and port numbers identify units but are excluded from model inputs.
evaluation: Disjoint five-tuple grouped holdout within each capture, with split seeds 7919, 104729, 130363
Common empirical-population drift control and disjoint-reference-pool stress test
All-opportunity and observed-only recall; sampling/timeout fragmentation; unit-weight ablation
reporting: Report every configured setting, including unsuccessful adaptations. Use paired contrasts and capture-level aggregation; do not count sampling seeds as independent real-world deployments. Distinguish empirical resampling from chronological field operation. No claims of line-rate deployment.
constraints: Only genuine public packet captures and their published labels. No raw data row deletion as a proxy for packet sampling. No held-out target labels in model fitting or threshold selection. Public dataset labels are inherited, not asserted independently verified.
packet_label_rule: A communication window is malicious if it contains any packet labeled malicious; a benign window contains only labeled benign packets. IoT-23 windows containing unmatched packets are excluded. This rule retains benign responses to malicious requests. Fixed before fitting any detector.
source_calibration_partition: All windows sharing a canonical five-tuple within a source capture stay together in either training or calibration.
data_scope: Eight IoT-23 captures and four Kitsune captures with per-file raw capture size below 1 GiB, fixed before model evaluation. IoT-23 capture 44 is excluded by this size limit.
design_history: The data eligibility, packet-label rule, measurement grid, and classifier baselines were fixed before classifier fitting. Grouped holdout and the common-population drift control were added after the initial held-out-capture and disjoint-pool analyses. This is an exploratory empirical study.
prediction: Training uses two tree workers per process. Prediction uses a fixed serial tree-summation order to make strict threshold ties reproducible.
